verdicts.summary: The clause handles the one-level case correctly. The first OR branch (already armed) does not use it, which matches the test and the commit's intent. The wake-hint query only reads threads that are already armed, so an excluded child does not cause a hot re-sweep. A thread.* event on the parent invalidates the due hint.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) The parent settles after the child failed but before it was armed: the next sweep reads the parent's override and does not arm the child. (2) The parent is later unsettled (override 'active'): '= settled' is false, so the child is armed again if the reset is no more than 24h overdue (MAX_OVERDUE_ARM_MS). (3) The wake-hint query might keep returning the excluded child's past resetAt and loop: it only selects limitRecovery.autoResume=1, so an unarmed child is ignored. (4) Malformed or missing lineage: json_extract gives NULL, the EXISTS subquery is false, and the child is armed as before.

verdicts.summary: The check looks only at the direct parent. A grandchild subagent whose root ancestor is settled is still auto-armed and resumed if its own parent (a subagent) is not settled.
verdicts.scenario: 1. Root R has subagent M, and M has subagent G. 2. R is settled. thread.settle does not cascade to subagents (Orchestrator.ts:3485-3504), so M keeps settledOverride null. 3. G hits a usage limit. Its parent M is not settled, so the NOT EXISTS clause at ProjectionStore.ts:3978-3983 passes and G is armed. 4. At reset, G is resumed and finishes. If delivering G's result starts a run on M, and M's completion is delivered to R, then R wakes. That is the same abandoned-work wake-up this commit is meant to prevent.
verdicts.missing: I did not trace whether delivering a subagent result to M (the getRecoveryThreadIds 'subagent-results' / delegated-completion path, ProjectionStore.ts:4071-4099) starts a new run on M, or whether M's completion then reaches the settled root R.
